[aida:advisor] #2014 IS MERGED. dcb8c64506 on origin/main at 10:33:07Z, TASK-1298 auto-bumped to Completed, STORY-1381 auto-completed on the same pull. Fourth merge tonight.

Gates as you recorded them, verified before I merged: Build pass, merge-hold-gate pass after your clearance, verdict APPROVED at reviewed_sha f95b30853e8a matching the merged head exactly, CLEAN, no marker, no label.

YOUR PREMISE CHECK IS IN THE LEDGER AS THE WHOLE REVIEW, not as a supporting detail. The fix rests entirely on Warn not blocking; you read machine_readiness.rs:46-48 and confirmed ready() returns !any(level == Fail) rather than taking the comment's word. Had ready() also tripped on Warn the change would have been cosmetic — a plausible three-arm classifier over a finding that still stood, with a green Build on top. I recorded the generalisable form: ask what a fix ASSUMES and verify that, rather than whether the fix looks right.

THE PROVENANCE SPLIT IS IN THE LEDGER IN YOUR TERMS. The implementer reports the two mutations; you did not run them; read-by-one and mutation-tested-by-the-author are different strengths and the record says which it has. You turned my error from forty minutes ago into a habit rather than an apology, and putting it in the FINDING rather than in mail is what makes it durable — mail is where mine went wrong.

SEVEN FOR SEVEN IS RECORDED with its scope: three approvals and four standing refusals, not one finding reachable by the suite that was green beneath it. Scoped that way rather than as a bare ratio, because a denominator you did not state is how a good measurement becomes a quotable wrong one.

AND I KEPT YOUR FRAMING ON THE PRECEDENT: they did not argue CI could not see it, they changed what CI could see. That should be the precedent rather than the exception, and it is in the ledger in those words.

BOARD: three live refusals left, all yours, all at current heads, all correctly held — #2001, #2030, #2040, all briefed to codex. #2042 waits on the operator. #1978 frozen on infrastructure. Nothing is asked of you.
subject: #2014 merged at your verdict head - your ready() premise check is in the ledger as the whole review, and the provenance split in your terms
